scope: Shared strict instant/calendar vocabulary required by the current durable Schedule domain

paired.method: Actual fixed util/time instant.ts with Temporal/Intl versus Native; exact values, rejection reasons, unsupported-zone cause and invalid-calendar/zone error names.

verification.native: 11 passed: new strict helper observations, never-throw formatting and historical Schedule regressions.

behavior: ASCII strict calendar and RFC3339 parsers distinguish malformed text, nonexistent dates, out-of-range fields and invalid offsets. Canonical UTC requires mandatory milliseconds and an exact four-digit-year round trip.

Integer Gregorian epoch arithmetic and manual canonical formatting avoid Windows CRT limits and year-padding behavior. Formatting refuses booleans, nonnumbers, fractions, infinity and values outside the four-digit bounds without throwing.

Zone identity follows the pinned ICU vocabulary. Local resolution rejects forward gaps and chooses the earlier overlap; checked cases include half-hour transitions, a skipped date, historic second offsets and both four-digit edges.

Extended-year resolution uses proleptic Gregorian arithmetic and a 400-year mapping for ZoneInfo future rules; checked years -1, 0, 10000 and 10004 in UTC, Shanghai and New York. Temporal's absolute epoch bound is enforced.
diagnostics: The first pairing exposed a mistaken assumption about JavaScript terminal dollar: without multiline mode Source rejects trailing line terminators. Native now uses strict end-of-input; original failed observations remain retained.

cleanup.retained: Source/Native observations, first failed comparison, commands, logs/XML and input hashes; synthetic short workspaces, homes and temporary directories removed.

limitations: Finite checked contracts do not establish equivalence for every IANA historical/future transition or arbitrary malformed Temporal object coercion.

Current Schedule persistence, recurrence, runtime and tool integration remain pending. This is targeted dependency verification, not complete regression, Portable/browser/Win7 acceptance or upstream promotion.
